title: Data acquisition for the development of a voice-controlled ultrasound robotic platform within the SURREAL project (SURREAL: Voice-Controlled Ultrasound Robotic Platform for Efficient Assistance in Liver Examination and Intervention)
summary: Ultrasound plays an important role in the diagnosis and treatment of many diseases. Particularly during complex interventional procedures and surgeries, its use requires considerable experience and close collaboration among medical staff. The aim of this study is therefore to establish the basis for an AI-assisted, voice-controlled ultrasound robot that can support medical staff during procedures. The study will investigate how reliably typical voice commands can be recognized in operating and interventional rooms and how they can be linked to corresponding ultrasound probe movements and image data. For this purpose, ultrasound images, ultrasound probe movements and verbal communication between the treating staff will be recorded and linked during planned procedures. In addition, the study will investigate which microphone position provides optimal speech intelligibility while minimizing background noise. The collected data will subsequently be used to develop an AI-based learning model for natural language control of the ultrasound robot.
conditions: The study investigates human-machine interaction during ultrasound-guided interventional procedures, with a focus on the integration of imaging data, movement patterns and verbal communication to identify reproducible interaction patterns.

interventions.name: During the planned surgical or interventional procedure, ultrasound images, changes in image motion and verbal communication between the treating physicians will be recorded and linked. In addition, the intelligibility of the recorded communication will be assessed depending on microphone positionin

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a clinical indication for an intervention or surgical procedure that is planned independently of the study and performed at the study site, who, following appropriate informed consent, provide written consent to participate in the study and to the collection of study data.
Exclusion criteria:
Withdrawal of informed consent
Insufficient comprehensibility of language or communication with the patients (inability to provide informed consent)
Inability to perform data collection (technical problems)
